title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page does not fit the surrounding cote. It is not part of Grothendieck's French manuscript on motivic Galois groups: the neighbouring pages 182 and 184 deal with motivic R-points, polarisations and torsion by H^1(R, G^ad). Page 183 is instead page 73 of an English typescript, typewritten with handwritten formulas. It reads like a translation, probably from Russian. The phrasing 'here r' is such', 'at n >= ...' and 'requirements 1') and 2') (See p. 202)' points that way, and the notation [nE] and O_V[nE] for the line bundle of a divisor and its sheaf of sections is Kodaira/Russian-school style. It was apparently misfiled in this folder; the archive number 183 is pencilled bottom left.

Mathematical content: V is a projective variety, E a divisor, and E_phi a member of a family of subvarieties (likely a divisor in |E| or a hyperplane-type section). From an earlier sequence (16), 0 -> O_V(-E_phi) -> O_V -> O_{E_phi} -> 0, twisting by [nE] gives sequence (17): 0 -> O_V(-E_phi)[nE] -> O_V[nE] -> O_{E_phi}[nE]|_{E_phi} -> 0. The map r' is restriction of local sections, given by its action on stalks. The long exact cohomology sequence (18) runs H^0(V, O[nE]) -> H^0(E_phi, O[nE]|) -> H^1(V, O(-E_phi)[nE]) -> H^1(V, O[nE]) -> H^1(E_phi, O[nE]|).

The text then chooses n(E_phi) so that, for n >= n(E_phi), the pair (E_phi, [nE]|_{E_phi}) satisfies 'requirements 1') and 2')'. These are presumably vanishing of higher cohomology and/or very ampleness / base-point freeness. Their existence follows from 'non-degeneracy' (i.e. ampleness) of [E] restricted to E_phi, which is Serre's theorem on the lower-dimensional variety. With n_E = max(n'', n(E_phi)), the argument continues on the next typescript page, which is not provided here.

This is the standard induction-on-dimension step. If E_phi ~ E, then O(-E_phi)[nE] = O[(n-1)E], so h^1(nE) <= h^1((n-1)E) for large n. The h^1 eventually stabilises, which forces surjectivity of restriction of global sections, and hence projective embedding or vanishing for V. This is the classical argument behind Kodaira/Serre/Nakai/Zariski-type results.
errors: No mathematical error is visible on this fragment; the argument is standard and incomplete on this page.
Typographical: the last term is written 'H.^1' with a stray dot.
The cross-reference 'See p. 202' does not match the typescript's own pagination (73). It likely refers to the pagination of the original source text or book.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is apparently a misfiled page from an English translation of someone else's text on cohomology of line bundles, not Grothendieck's motivic notes. Its content is the textbook restriction-sequence step of a Serre/Kodaira-type ampleness argument. Nothing here is new or attributable to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: The subscript on script E in the running text is typed as a small symbol resembling 'ꝏ'. The handwritten formulas show it is phi, so E_phi throughout is correct.
The handwritten map in (18) is labelled r^* (or r with a star above), consistent with the transcription.
The last term of (18) is written 'H.^1(E_phi, ...)' in the image, a stray dot, i.e. H^1.
The archive number '183' is pencilled at the bottom left of the page, and the typescript page number is 73 at the top right.
